title: Building Teens on a Ten Frame

steps.body: The ten-frame turns any teen into a picture: the full frame is the ten, and the dots outside are the ones.
steps.narration: The ten-frame turns any teen into a picture: the full frame is the ten, and the dots outside are the ones.

widget.prompt: Fifteen is a full ten and five more. Tap to build those five extra dots.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 5 dots still missing — five taps build the extras that make fifteen.
4 leaves 1 dot still missing — one more tap completes the five extras.
6 adds 1 too many — only 5 extra dots are what fifteen needs.

widget.missFeedback: You already know the ten is done; tap 5 dots for the extras that make fifteen.
widget.successFeedback: The 5 extras are built — one complete ten and 5 more is exactly what fifteen means.

predict.prompt: A full frame and 5 loose dots — how do you read it?

options.label: Ten at a glance, then count 5
Count all fifteen dots one by one

predict.reveal: The full frame is a known ten; counting it dot by dot wastes the frame's whole gift.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb build teen.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb build teen rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: A teen has one full ten and six loose dots. Build only the loose part.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 6 dots still missing — six taps build the loose part of sixteen.
5 leaves 1 dot still missing — one more tap completes the six loose dots.
7 adds 1 too many — only 6 loose dots are the loose part of sixteen.

widget.missFeedback: You already know the ten is done; tap 6 dots for the loose part of sixteen.
widget.successFeedback: The 6 loose dots are built — one complete ten and 6 more is exactly what sixteen means.

steps.body: Reading the picture is instant — nobody counts a full frame. Ten at a glance, then count only the extras.
steps.narration: Reading the picture is instant — nobody counts a full frame. Ten at a glance, then count only the extras.

widget.prompt: A learner reads 18 as eight tens and one one. It is really one ten and eight ones — build just the eight loose ones to repair the model.

commonCounts.feedback: That shows one too few loose ones. The target needs 8.
That shows one too many loose ones. Stop at 8.

widget.missFeedback: Build exactly 8 loose ones to repair the model; the ten stays fixed at just one.
widget.successFeedback: The 8 loose ones are built — with the finished ten, that makes 18.

widget.prompt: A group shows 16 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extras reaches 16.
Correct — a full ten and 6 more is what the numeral 16 says: 1 ten, 6 ones.
6 counts only the extras and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 6. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 15 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 16.
17 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 6 hops from 10 to land on 16.

widget.missFeedback: Count 6 on from 10: you land on 16.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 6 more is 16 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 6 counts past ten are needed to reach 16.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 6 numbers, on 16.

widget.prompt: A carton holds ten eggs and three sit beside it. Build the three extras.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 3 dots still missing — three taps build the extras beside the carton's ten.
2 leaves 1 dot still missing — one more tap completes the three extras.
4 adds 1 too many — only 3 extra dots sit beside the ten.

widget.missFeedback: You already know the carton's ten is done; tap 3 dots for the extras beside it.
widget.successFeedback: The 3 extras are built — one complete ten and 3 more is exactly what thirteen means.
